title: Math/physics invariants and speed paths
checked_ok: _SoftClip backward is the true derivative of its forward: for |x| > T, t = (|y|-T)/(A-T) = tanh(u), so dy/dx = 1 - t^2; for |x| <= T it clamps to 0, giving slope 1. It is C1 at |x| = T (verified numerically at T-1e-9, T, T+1e-9, -T). In the mixed finite/inf case As=1 is a harmless placeholder and torch.where(fin, d, g) restores the identity gradient. gradcheck (fp64, CPU) passes for knee in {0, 0.5} x mixed in {False, True}.

_clip saturation fraction bookkeeping: the reshape to (2L, H), the sum over H and the division by E*27*H are correct per (alpha/beta, layer) group. B1 clip acts only on the geometry path, so the q-path stays linear.

load_compat / _node_in (B2): the old checkpoint's node_in.0.weight is zero-padded at the end. _node_in multiplies the first in_features-NF2 columns with [nfeat, agg] and the last NF2 with nfeat2, so zero columns reproduce the old function exactly. bnd_* buffers missing from the sd keep the model values. The post-load hook refreshes _bst/_rw_fin.

O_h rotate_nd is an exact change of frame and nothing is rotated twice or skipped: grid g' = R(g-n)+n; cells c' = (R(2c+1-n)+n-1)/2 (integer for n=32); slot permutation offs[t] = R(o-1)+1 (derived from g' = 2c'+1+R(o-1)); moments M'[a'] = prod s_i^{a'_i} M[b], with b[p_i] = a'_i from (R xi)_i = s_i xi_{p_i} and |det R|=1; gp_faces axis b = argsort(p)[a] with an owner/nbr swap when s_b<0 (owner stays the lower cell, which the face stencil in _face_setup assumes); diag3 -> s_i s_j D[p_i,p_j] = R D R^T; normal -> R n; offset + (sum n' - sum n)/2 from n'.x' = n.x + (sum n' - sum n)/2; taus corner permutation; node flags unchanged.

O_h q in/out: rot_dofs(qd, p, s) = (I x R) qd and rot_dofs(., argsort(p), s[argsort(p)]) = (I x R^T). The rigid split and port overwrite are applied in the original frame. The view's MGCache, face stencil, feat_v2 features (rho via the cube-symmetric D_full, s, hop, plane, box) and fringe masks are all built from the rotated nd with a distinct case key.

Variational upper bound in the forward-energy path: Geo.field (and oh._field) returns an admissible field with u_P = q exactly (fp32-rounded q). The rigid part RA c is in the null space of K (GP gradient jumps vanish for linear fields). So e_hat = u^T K u >= q^T S q under every feature (O_h, B1, B2, fringe_soft fade, fused kernels, TF32). Only the adjoint-based apply is affected (INVARIANTS-2).

fastnet ext_T is the exact algebraic transpose of ext (up to rounding): port clamp adjoint (X0b += Xb*pm; A = Xb*(1-pm)); hyperedge layers (S,G / St,Gt, and W^T); U-Net skip bookkeeping (gskip per level, Rt and gskip on the way back); gates applied before conv_transpose3d, with the same weight tensor as the conv3d adjoint (padding 1); restriction rv = t_w*w/den and prolongation with the skip scale folded in; W_in/W_out; field_T = yP + (I - RPpinv^T RP^T) ext_T(yI) + RPpinv^T RA^T yI.
fastnet matches MGNO2.forward layer order, mask and fade handling: face layer index gl, fringe elements with xab/Wx/c.deg, fringe faces masked then b*gp_fade, and el_fade applied to the masked b.

sparse_layers.HyperFn gradients: dZ' = S^T dY, dW = sum Z^T dZ', dZ = dZ' W^T, dX = G^T dZ, da = <X[n], dZ[h,e]>, db = <dY[n]/deg, Z'[h,e]> via SDDMM on the p1 pattern with the inverse permutation fa[p1] = va. No duplicate nodes within a hyperedge (27 element nodes; face stencil = owner layers 1-2 + neighbour layer 1).

fused_hyper kernels: gather/scatter/backward formulas match HyperFn (the DEG flag applies 1/deg[n] on the b side only). Offsets n*BF and (h*Eh+e)*BF are computed in int64; (e*S+s)*H fits in int32 at current sizes. Column masking uses other=0. Atomic partial sums for dA/dB over column blocks are correct. Empty hyperedge set (Eh=0) or BF=0 returns zeros or empty tensors in both forward and backward. H must be a power of 2 (H=4), and violating that fails at compile time, not silently. Inputs a/b/Zp/dZ are made contiguous before the kernels.

cert.py: Delta = u^T K u - q^T S q = r_I^T K_II^-1 r_I (with e_P = 0 and (K u*)_I = 0). The one-vector bound (x^T r)^2/(x^T K_II x) holds for any x (Cauchy-Schwarz), so the final re-evaluation makes the Krylov/CG/Jacobi bounds rigorous whatever the basis rounding or eigenvalue floors. eps >= Delta_lb/(e_hat - Delta_lb) follows from monotonicity. The lattice_lower identity C - C_hat = sum Delta_c + |U* - U_hat|_K^2 is correct for an exact, symmetric K_hat. node_blocks symmetrises the upper CSR correctly. Host eigh is only a device workaround.
bank_ritz returns true Rayleigh quotients (renormalised with the unfloored G), so ritz <= mu. tail_loss flooring only lowers eigenvalues for near-dependent directions (conservative).

Anti-drift rule: MGNO/MGNO2 forward, oh._field and fastnet ext/ext_T contain no factorisation, solve or residual iteration. The exact Neumann factor (adversarial first visit, worst_ratio) and cert are used only for data and monitoring outside the forward. fastnet.s_hat uses only a K product (the variational readout).
fp32 matmuls (bmm, cuBLAS) are not TF32 (matmul.allow_tf32 default False, never set). Only cuDNN convs are affected.

items.title: B1 saturation metric does not see the knee band, so 'clip never triggered / identity in-distribution' is not established
items.claim: With bound_knee = k > 0 the soft clip stops being the identity at |x| > T = k*A, but the saturation count (_clip line 413: `(x.abs() > A)`, _transfer line 430: `(sp[j] > A)`) only counts |x| > A. For the c_b1 arm (A = 2 x training max, knee 0.5, so T = the calibration max) the whole band T < |x| <= 2T is compressed without being counted. The logged value sat_max = 0 therefore only shows |x| <= 2T. It does not show that B1 acted as the identity.
items.evidence: g_b1.sh: `b[k] = torch.as_tensor(2.0 * mx)` with the rule 'A = 2 x max over the 40 calibration training geometries; use with bound_knee = 0.5 (identity up to the training max)'. _SoftClip forward: `torch.where(ax > T, sign(x)*(T + (As-T)*tanh((ax-T)/(As-T))), x)`. At |x| = 1.5T it outputs 1.462T (2.5% low), and at |x| = A = 2T it outputs T(1+tanh 1) = 1.762T (11.9% low). The counter stays at 0 across that whole range. Also: T is the max over only 40 training geometries under v1 snap_60000 weights, while c_b1 trained 15k more steps (lr 3e-4) over the full pool. train3 logs sat_max only every log_every=50 steps (train3.py:720-721), for the current training geometry only. V2 doc line 13/19: 'sat_max 全程 0（截断从未触发）' and 'B1 在分布内等价于恒等映射（零代价的分布外保险）'.
items.consequence: The v2 claim that B1 is exactly the identity in-distribution, and so zero-cost insurance, is unsupported. The measured arm neutrality is still valid, but the reason given for it is not proven. The same blind spot makes sat_stats a poor OOD detector in deployment: a geometry can have coefficients compressed by up to ~12% while reporting sat_max = 0.
items.fix: In _clip/_transfer, count |x| > knee*A (the 'knee' fraction) separately from |x| > A, and report both from sat_stats. Before writing 'identity in-distribution' into v2, re-run calib_b1 capture on the c_b1 best/last checkpoint over all train, val and gate geometries, and report max|x|/T per group.

verification.reasoning: The code matches the claim. In models.py, _clip counts `(x.abs() > A)` and _transfer counts `(sp[j] > A)`, but when bound_knee > 0, _SoftClip starts compressing at |x| > T = knee*A. Nothing counts the band T < |x| <= A. g_b1.sh builds bounds_B1.pt as `2.0 * mx` and sets c_b1.json bound_knee = 0.5, so T equals the calibration max and A = 2T. My hand check of the compression figures agrees: at 1.5T the output is T + T*tanh(0.5) = 1.462T, and at 2T it is T(1 + tanh 1) = 1.762T. sat_stats documents itself as a 'fraction of |a_raw| > A', and train3 logs only sat_max (train3.py:720-721). No other check anywhere compares |x| against T: calib_b1.py and t_models_v2*.py test only sat_max == 0 or <= 0.01. Doc lines 13 and 19 say 'sat_max 全程 0（截断从未触发）' and 'B1 在分布内等价于恒等映射'. Those statements need |x| <= T, which the logged metric cannot show. The measured neutrality of the arm is unaffected. What is unsupported is the stated reason for it, and the counter's value as an OOD score in deployment. I kept it major because v2 adopts B1 on the basis of that invariant and names sat_stats as its OOD monitor. No gate number is wrong.

items.title: cuDNN TF32 conv: the reaction op.apply = E'^T K E is not the variational readout, and the gate, A7 metrics and deployment still run this way
items.claim: torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 is never set (the only occurrence is diag_tf32.py, which restores the default). So conv3d in the forward E and conv_transpose3d (fastnet.ext_T) or cuDNN backward-data (trainlib.s_hat_apply autograd) in the adjoint E' are different TF32-rounded maps. Every reaction used by the lattice is apply(q) = E'^T K E q. It is not symmetric, and q^T apply(q) = (E'q)^T K (Eq) is not guaranteed >= q^T S q. The variational upper bound holds only for the forward energy u^T K u.
items.evidence: evalnet.NetOp.apply -> geo.s_hat_apply (0.5 * autograd grad of energy: backward conv in TF32). FastOp.apply -> fast.s_hat -> field_T -> _conv(transpose=True) -> Fn.conv_transpose3d. lattice3.evaluate uses op.apply as the PCG matvec, and _measure_ computes energy via op.apply. lat_full.cell_metrics: `eps[i] = (q * op.apply(q)).sum(0) / E[i] - 1` and `bound_holds`. cert.lattice_lower assumes K_hat = sum S_hat_c symmetric with K_hat U_hat = f. bench_deploy: `e_hat = (Q * fast.s_hat(Q)).sum(0)`. Measured asymmetry (V2 doc sec. 4): 1.4e-3 on r1 with TF32 vs 7.6e-6 fp32.
items.consequence: Gate compliance, A7 eps/w/bound_holds/additivity and the deployment energy ratios (1.008 / 1.015) all carry an adjoint-path error of up to ~1e-3 relative, which is not variational. For cells or directions with eps below ~1e-3 (FULL neighbours, near-rigid loads), eps can go negative and bound_holds can fail spuriously. CG theory does not apply to an asymmetric matvec. That matters little with the exact preconditioner (13 iterations) but does matter for the deployable Jacobi-PCG runs (2149-2524 iterations, V2 doc sec. 6). It does not change the <=3% gate verdicts at current margins.
items.fix: Add an explicit precision flag (e.g. env OPL_CONV_FP32=1, or fastnet.FP32_CONV) that sets torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=False around FastNet/NetOp evaluation and in bench_deploy/lat_full. Record the flag in every gate JSON. Decide the v2 default explicitly: fp32 cost is 2-37% on s_hat. For monitoring, report forward-energy eps (u^T K u with u = op.field(q)) next to the apply-based eps in lat_full.

verification.reasoning: The defect is real by default, but part of the evidence and most of the proposed fix are wrong. Correction: allow_tf32 is set in more places than diag_tf32.py. models.py:36-45 defines set_conv_fp32() and reads env OPL_CONV_FP32=1, and train1.py/train3.py honour a cfg key conv_fp32. That already covers most of the suggested fix. What remains true: (a) the flag is off by default, and no run script in the scratchpad sets OPL_CONV_FP32 or conv_fp32; (b) evalnet.py, lat_full.py, bench_deploy.py and eval_views.py never read cfg['conv_fp32'], so gate, A7 and deployment evaluations use TF32 unless the env var is exported; (c) no gate JSON records the setting. trainlib.Geo.s_hat_apply returns 0.5*autograd grad of u^T K u, so the adjoint goes through cuDNN dgrad. fastnet uses conv_transpose3d. With TF32 both paths give E'^T K E with E' != E, and lattice3._measure_ and lat_full.cell_metrics compute energy and eps from op.apply. On the consequence: lat_full sets eps = 0 for exact cells, and the gate neighbour is exact, so the 'FULL neighbours go negative' case does not apply. Learned cut cells have eps at percent level against an error of about 1e-3. Spurious negative eps or bound_holds failures are therefore unlikely at current margins, and the <=3% verdicts do not change. Downgraded to minor: the flag exists, and what is missing is wiring it into the eval scripts and recording it.

items.title: Gate pass ignores PCG convergence
items.claim: lattice3.evaluate returns pcg_residual, but compare() computes gate_pass only from compliance and sensitivity errors of the final iterate X. If PCG stops at maxit (400 in evalnet/lat_full) without reaching tol, the gate is scored on an unconverged lattice solution with no flag.
items.evidence: `out['gate_pass'] = bool(ce[g].max() <= 0.03 and np.nanmax(vec[:, g]) <= 0.03)`. pcg_residual is never read in compare(), evalnet or lat_full.summarize (only pcg_iterations is printed).
items.consequence: With the exact dense preconditioner and a symmetric operator this is harmless (about 13 iterations). With a badly trained cell (large mu), the TF32 asymmetry (INVARIANTS-2), or a future deployable preconditioner, a non-converged run could pass or fail the gate silently.
items.fix: Add pcg_converged = pcg_residual < tol (or < 1e-8) to compare(). Make gate_pass require it, or at least report it next to gate_pass in evalnet/lat_full output.

verification.reasoning: lattice3.evaluate (tol=1e-10, default maxit=300; 400 from evalnet, lat_full and run_lat) exits the loop at maxit without raising. It then measures compliance and sensitivities on the last iterate X and stores pcg_residual. compare() copies only pcg_iterations, and gate_pass = ce[g].max() <= 0.03 and nanmax(vec[:, g]) <= 0.03 never uses the residual. A grep finds no reader of pcg_residual in evalnet.py, lat_full.py, run_lat.py or compare_arms.py. bench_deploy passes the residual into compare() but compare ignores it. The gate can therefore be scored on an unconverged solve with nothing flagging it. With the exact Cholesky preconditioner it converges in about 13 iterations today, so the risk is latent. Minor.

items.title: _SoftClip has no guard for A <= 0 or knee >= 1; the B1 bounds file drops calib's inf-for-empty-group rule; the knee is not stored with the bounds
items.claim: The backward computes t = (|y| - T)/(A - T). If A = 0 this is 0/0, and clamp_ keeps the NaN, so the gradient is NaN. If knee = 1 it divides by zero. calib_b1 sets empty groups to inf (`torch.where(q['count'] > 0, mu * q['p999'], inf)`), but g_b1.sh rebuilt bounds_B1.pt as `2.0 * mx`, which would give A = 0 for a group with no samples. Separately, bound_knee is a model_arg that is not stored in the bounds file or in state_dict. Loading bounds_B1.pt without bound_knee=0.5 silently gives the plain tanh A tanh(x/A), which is 7.6% low at x = train max, instead of the identity the file's 'rule' string promises.
items.evidence: CPU check (<1 s): `_SoftClip.apply(torch.tensor([0.,0.3]), torch.tensor(0.), False, 0.5)` gives forward [0, 0] and grad [nan, nan]. gradcheck passes for knee 0 / 0.5, mixed True / False, and at |x| = T. g_b1.sh line 13 carries the knee only as a comment string. models.py line 326 keeps `self.bound_knee` as a plain attribute.
items.consequence: Not triggered in the current runs: all ab/fab/xab/rw groups are populated, and c_b1's cfg carries knee 0.5. But a v2 config that combines O_h + B1 and copies bounds= without bound_knee trains a different function. A future bounds file with an empty group would produce NaN geometry-path gradients, which the NONFINITE_GRAD guard then skips every step.
items.fix: In set_bounds, reject A <= 0 and 0 < knee < 1 violations. Store the knee inside the bounds file and in a buffer (e.g. bnd_knee), and warn or raise when a bounds file with a knee rule is loaded with bound_knee = 0. In g_b1-style rules, keep the inf for count == 0.

verification.reasoning: _SoftClip.backward computes t = ((|y| - T)/(As - T)).clamp_(0, 1), and clamp propagates NaN. So A = 0 with knee 0.5 gives 0/0 = NaN, and knee = 1 gives a zero denominator. The knee = 0 path has the same problem: tanh_backward(g, y/A) with A = 0 is NaN. set_bounds does no validation. calib_b1.calibrate maps count == 0 to inf. g_b1.sh bypasses that rule with `2.0 * mx`, and _Hist.mx starts at 0, so an empty group (or one that is all zero) gets A = 0. bound_knee is a plain attribute (models.py:453). It is not a buffer and is not saved in bounds_B1.pt, which carries it only in the 'rule' string. Loading bounds_B1.pt without bound_knee = 0.5 silently gives plain A*tanh(x/A): at x = T = A/2 that is A*tanh(0.5) = 0.924T, i.e. 7.6% low. train3 has a NONFINITE_GRAD skip guard (line 709), so NaN gradients would skip steps silently rather than crash. None of this is triggered in current runs, since the populated groups cannot be checked remotely and c_b1 carries knee 0.5. It is a latent robustness gap. Minor.

title: Data v2 generation (prep_geo2)
checked_ok: Traction face quadrature matches lattice3.face_traction_weights: h = 1/(6n) midpoint grid, weight h^2 N_i, material filter |phi| <= trilinear tau, cut half-space normal.x <= offset only for cut cells, points in inactive elements dropped. On box faces the Q2 shape values off the face are exactly 0 at xi in {0,1}, so only face (box) nodes receive force.
Traction.forces layout: (m,3,k) -> A @ (m,3k) -> (N,3,k) -> node-major xyz port DOFs, consistent with C.P ordering (port_node_ids = nodes[onport], P = nonzero(repeat(onport,3))).
Cut-surface point x0 = n_hat*offset/|normal| lies on normal.x = offset, consistent with moments_ad psi3 = offset - n.x.
force_c 10% cut mask per sample; face_c rigid removal on the loaded face nodes makes the resultant and moment zero, so the second projection in C.neumann is a no-op (the consistency issue is DATA-2).

support_k: alpha = 0.3*10^U in [0.3, 3), log-uniform, one per face; k_i = alpha*K_ii added on all box port DOFs of the face; springs on all 3 components over a material face make the system SPD; fp64 factor (_spd64) with Jacobi scaling including the springs; loads only on the other faces, cut band free; non-finite solutions raise.

glued absolute node keys: W = 6n+1 over [-2n, 4n]^3 is collision-free and int64; shared nodes found by searchsorted on the sorted test keys; neighbour-own nodes appended; the upper CSR is rebuilt by min/max and unique; the keep renumbering is monotone, so upper stays upper; nnz and index ranges fit int32 CSR.

glued faces: tface/nglue/nfar are correct for sgn > 0 and sgn < 0; the far face is clamped (DOFs dropped) or on springs k = alpha*diag with alpha in [0.3, 3); test cut band and other box faces free; loads only on free faces of both cells; 25% neighbour-only via (1 - only_n) on the test loads only; q = u[Ct.P] in the test's own numbering.
Shared DOFs on the glue plane (box nodes, fringe nodes included) match lattice3's port-level gluing by absolute position; cut-only private DOFs cannot coincide with neighbour nodes.
Offsets exclude -x/-y (the gate's), so no gate configuration is generated.

family_full: name-prefix family 'fresh_<split>_<dddd>' + '_full' (rotated: the rotated FULL or skip). make_split splits by family, so the FULL parent always sits in the same split as its cut cell. No cross-split leakage through the glued neighbour, and val geometries' glued banks are used only in their own val metrics.

Unit-energy normalisation: rigid removal with the port rigid basis, energy via the refined interior factor (fp32 + 3 fp64 refinement steps); F = (K E q)_P in fp64, stored fp32; unit_energy_check in DONE2; zero-direction guard before normalisation.
Sensitivity labels: sens2 on u = C.extend(q) with dM from central differences at taus0, the same as prep_geo; saved in fp64.
--F-old: F = S q computed from the stored fp32 q (exact for the stored bank); NaN columns kept NaN and filtered by HostBanks.clean; only writes new *_F.npy files.
--fix-support never deletes: it renames to *.nan_bak.npy (failure-path issue in DATA-4) and recomputes with the same prep_geo definition using fp64 spring factors.
_spd_glued: fp64, then fp64 retry after freeing the cache, then fp32 only on memory errors; non-memory errors propagate; normalisation, sens and F always use the test cell's own exact factor.

y load-6 rise in the r2 pilot: no y-specific defect found in prep_geo2 (force_c, face_c and support_k are symmetric across axes). Plausible data-side contributors are the uniform-nodal component of force_c/face_c (DATA-2) and the geometry-dependent glued BC mix (DATA-6); class-mix dilution of 'face' is on the trainer side.

items.title: Every fresh_* geometry gets the same RNG seed, so all geometries share one set of random load functions
items.claim: The per-case seed is `(int.from_bytes(case.encode(), 'little') + 7919) % 2**31`. Bytes are little-endian and the modulus is 2^31, so the seed depends only on the first 4 characters of the case name. Every case starting with 'fresh' gets the same seed, 1936036181. prep_geo.py:225 has the same collision (1936028262), so the old classes have it too.
items.evidence: Local check: 'fresh_train_0020_cover01_r2', 'fresh_train_0020_full', 'fresh_development_0002_full' and 'fresh_train_0031_cover01_r1_rotgeneral' all give 1936036181 with the +7919 form. plane_waves and patches are functions of absolute position X. How many random numbers they draw does not depend on X; torch.randint on the CUDA generator advances by a fixed amount whatever the range. So sample j of force_c, face_c, support_k or glued uses the same wave vectors, phases, amplitudes, patch widths, spring alpha and randperm on every geometry with the same face set and the same --classes list. The streams only drift apart where the number of material faces differs.
items.consequence: Across roughly 150 geometries the training rows of each class are built from about 512 shared load functions, not independent draws. Family members (FULL, r1, r2) get almost identical traction fields on their shared faces. Held-out geometries are all scored on the same 64 'val' functions (rows 512..575), so class means over val geometries are strongly correlated. There is no train/val row overlap, but load diversity is much lower than intended and arm comparisons rest on correlated samples.
items.fix: Seed from a hash of the full name, e.g. int(hashlib.sha256(case.encode()).hexdigest()[:8],16) plus a class-specific offset. Use a separate generator per class so a class's samples do not depend on which other classes run in the same invocation (see DATA-8). Keep the old seed behind a flag if the old banks must be reproducible.

verification.reasoning: prep_geo2.py:409 computes `seed = (int.from_bytes(case.encode(), 'little') + 7919) % 2**31`. With little-endian bytes, the value mod 2^31 depends only on the first ~31 bits, i.e. the first four characters 'fres'. I reproduced it locally: all four example names give 1936036181, and the prep_geo.py:225 form gives 1936028262. All cases match the regex ^fresh_ (family_full), so all of them share one seed. In prep_data.plane_waves the draw sizes (randn/rand of kk x 3 x 48) do not depend on X. The wave vectors, amplitudes and phases (75% of every Traction.random block) are therefore the same functions of absolute position on every geometry with the same face set and cut status. The same holds for the spring alpha, the only_n masks and the randperm. Nuance: in patches the centre index comes from randint(0, X.shape[0]), so centres differ with the quadrature count, but widths and directions are shared. The streams drift apart once face sets differ, which the finding already says. Diversity across geometries is much lower than intended, and the same defect is in the old classes. The effect is common to all arms, so it correlates the samples but does not bias arm-vs-arm comparisons. Major is still fair.

items.title: force_c and face_c are equilibrated by a Euclidean rigid-mode projection, which adds non-consistent nodal loads on all ports (fringe and cut band included)
items.claim: force_c passes consistent tractions to C.neumann, which first does f - Q Q^T f (teacher.py:284). Q is the orthonormal rigid basis on ALL port nodes: box nodes, fictitious-fringe nodes and cut-band nodes. The net force and moment of the random tractions is removed by a uniform translation load plus a linear rotation load on every port DOF, not by adjusting the traction. face_c (line 168) does the same on T.nodes, which include fringe face nodes that have tiny consistent weights. So the docstring claim that fictitious-fringe nodes get almost nothing, and that the cut is unloaded in 90% of samples, does not hold for any sample with a nonzero resultant.
items.evidence: teacher.py:284 `f = f - self.Q @ (self.Q.T @ f)` with `self.Q = rigid_basis(self.port_node_ids, ...)`. The translation columns are uniform, 1/sqrt(N_ports) on every port node. prep_geo2.py:168 `F[dofs] = ff - Rf @ (Rf.T @ ff)`. A toy numpy check (<1 s) used the same plane_waves / patches generators on a 6-face node grid with no cut band. The removed part ||QQ^T f||/||f|| had a median of 0.35 for waves and 0.37 for patches. The average per-node correction was 0.36x (waves) and 1.2x (patches) of the average per-node load. On cut cells the correction also spreads onto the cut band and fringe nodes, which have no consistent load.
items.consequence: A large share of every force_c and face_c load is the rejected 'uniform nodal' pattern. That pattern is the stress test, not the gate. The r2-pilot result that consistent tractions help (compliance -15 to 28%) was measured with this mixed class, and part of the effect, including side effects on the gate's y load-6 sensitivity, may come from the uniform component rather than the consistent one. support_k and glued are not affected: they are supported and not projected.
items.fix: Equilibrate inside the traction space. With G = Q^T A (6 x 3m, the resultant and moment of the consistent nodal forces), set t <- t - G^T (G G^T)^-1 G t, or fit and subtract a rigid-like traction a + b x (x - x_c) over the loaded quadrature points. Then f = A t is both consistent and self-equilibrated, and C.neumann's projection becomes a no-op. Log ||QQ^T f||/||f|| as a check.

verification.reasoning: force_c (l.151) passes the raw sum of consistent face (and cut) forces to C.neumann. teacher.py:284 does `f = f - self.Q @ (self.Q.T @ f)`, where Q = rigid_basis(port_node_ids) is an orthonormal basis over ALL port nodes: box, fringe and cut band. The translation columns are uniform per node. The net force and moment are therefore removed by a uniform-nodal translation load plus a linear rotation load on every port DOF, including the fringe nodes and the cut band. face_c (l.168) does the same with Rf on T.nodes, which include fringe nodes that carry only tiny consistent weight. Its result is face-equilibrated, so the global projection in neumann becomes a no-op there. The docstring statements ('fictitious-fringe nodes get almost nothing', cut unloaded in 90%) describe f before the projection, not the load actually applied. The component is large, not a rounding term: plane_waves favour low wavenumbers (kmin 0.5, amp ~ mag^-beta) and Gaussian patches have a nonzero resultant by construction, so the reviewer's ~0.35 relative removed norm is plausible. Uniform forces on weakly stiff fringe nodes can then dominate the unit-energy normalisation. support_k and glued are supported and not projected, as the finding says. Confirmed as stated. Its link to the r2 y load-6 side effect remains a hypothesis.

items.title: The fp32 fallback of the two-cell factor has no refinement or accuracy check; glued directions can be dominated by solver noise
items.claim: _spd_glued falls back to an fp32 cuDSS factor of the Jacobi-scaled glued system (about 8e5 DOFs for FULL+FULL, which is the case for every FULL training geometry glued to itself). The solution at line 321 is used as-is: no fp64 iterative refinement, no residual check. After rigid removal and unit-energy normalisation, the test cell's elastic part can be small, especially in the 25% neighbour-only samples. fp32 error of order kappa*6e-8 is then amplified into the 'direction'.
items.evidence: Line 321: `u[keep] = sA[:, None] * sol.solve(sA[:, None] * F[keep])`. SPDSolver.solve casts to fp32 and back (teacher.py:78-80) and does no refinement. The only guard is `_finite` (line 322) plus the ZERO_DIRECTION test (1e-12 relative), neither of which measures accuracy. Precedent in this code base: fp32 spring factors produced the non-finite support banks that --fix-support now repairs with fp64.
items.consequence: Labels (S, F, energy) are exact for whatever q comes out, so nothing is mislabelled. But for FULL-FULL pairs the glued class can contain rough, noise-shaped unit-energy directions instead of lattice-context directions. That biases the class the v2 decision relies on, and it goes unnoticed because the only record is the precision tag.
items.fix: When precision == 'fp32', run 2-3 fp64 refinement steps using the glued upper CSR (r = F - K_glued u, u += solve(r)). This is data generation, not the network forward, so it is allowed. Log the relative residual per offset in DONE2 and reject or regenerate an offset whose residual exceeds, say, 1e-6.

verification.reasoning: The missing accuracy handling is real. _spd_glued falls back to an fp32 SPDSolver (fdt=float32), solve() casts to fp32 and back (teacher.py:78-80), and _glued_offsets l.366 uses the result directly. The only checks are _finite and the ZERO_DIRECTION guard, and there is no residual check. The claimed consequence does not follow from the code, though. A Cholesky solve is backward stable, so u solves a nearby (K + dK) system. The forward error concentrates in the soft modes of the supported two-cell system, which are smooth, so the directions are not 'noise-shaped'. Labels are exact for whatever q comes out. Two things decide whether the neighbour-only (25%) samples are materially degraded: whether the fp32 path is ever taken (only after two fp64 memory failures), and how large the Jacobi-scaled condition number is. Neither can be settled by reading. The GLUED_OFFSET precision tag is the only record. Adding fp64 refinement and a residual log is cheap and advisable, but the damage is unproven.

items.title: Glued far-face BC (clamp vs springs) is tied to the offset's list index, so per-axis coverage depends on geometry and is often the opposite of the gate

If +x has no material (e.g. a cut with normal ~x), +y moves to index 0 and becomes clamped. The gate (x and y) always clamps the neighbour's far face. So y-axis gluing with a clamped far face is absent for most geometries, while x has a clamped analogue.

For r2 itself +x may be empty, in which case +y is clamped, so this is not proven as the cause.
items.fix: Use both BCs for every offset (split each offset's samples half/half), or draw clamp/spring per chunk from gen. Record the realised per-axis mix in DONE2.

items.title: Cut-plane quadrature point differs between prep_geo2 (correct) and lattice3's reported cut loads (off-plane when |normal| != 1)
items.claim: prep_geo2 places the plane at x0 = n_hat * offset / |normal|, which satisfies normal.x = offset, the convention of moments (psi3 = offset - n.x, non-unit n) and of the _material half-space test. lattice3.plane_traction_weights uses `x0 = nrm * off` with unit nrm, i.e. the plane normal.x = |normal| * offset.
items.evidence: prep_geo2.py:87 `x0 = nrm * C.offset / np.linalg.norm(C.normal)` vs lattice3.py:36 `x0 = nrm * off`. The packet normals are not unit, e.g. seat100032 normal = [1, 1225339/15625000, 0], |n| = 1.00307, offset 0.545. The lattice3 plane is then shifted about 1.7e-3 (about 5% of an element) into the removed half-space. The shift grows with |n| - 1.
items.consequence: The cut-surface 'report' loads (not the gate) are integrated on a slightly different plane from the force_c cut loads used in training. This is a small, geometry-dependent inconsistency in the reported cut compliance and sensitivity numbers.
items.fix: In lattice3.plane_traction_weights use `x0 = nrm * off / np.linalg.norm(cell.normal)`, behind a flag if old report numbers must be reproduced. Better, share one quadrature routine (prep_geo2.Traction) between prep and gate.

verification.reasoning: prep_geo2.Traction (l.87) uses x0 = n_hat * offset / |normal|, the point where normal.x = offset. This is consistent with _material's `P @ normal <= offset` using the non-unit normal. lattice3.plane_traction_weights (l.36) uses x0 = n_hat * off, where n_hat.x = off, i.e. normal.x = |normal| * off. That point lies on the removed side, at distance off*(1 - 1/|n|) from the true plane. lattice3 applies no half-space test on that plane and only checks |phi| <= tau and that the element is active, so the shifted points are integrated. With |n| = 1.00307 and off = 0.545 the shift is about 1.7e-3, roughly 5% of an element of size 1/32. This affects only the cut-surface 'report' loads, not the gate.

title: Trainer v2 (train3 + trainlib host banks)
checked_ok: EMA update: torch._foreach_lerp_(shadow, params, 1-decay) = e + (1-d)(p-e) is correct. Parameter order and names match state_dict keys, and model_state keeps buffers (B1 bnd_*) raw. EMA.applied restores the raw weights bitwise. MGNO/MGNO2 recompute the geometry path from the parameters on every forward (no parameter-dependent caches; _pat caches only sparsity patterns), so swapping the EMA weights in is valid.

Checkpoint contents: best.pt/last.pt/snap 'model' = selected (EMA) weights plus model_raw and score_raw. ckpt.pt holds raw model, opt, sched, ema, qi, best and visits. evalnet/eval_views load ck['model'] = the selected weights.

Eval switches: eval_weights='sel' changes only which weight sets are evaluated at intermediate evals (score = res[sel]['score'] is unchanged, and the last eval runs all sets). cert_every affects reporting only (cert is not in score()). evaluate() consumes none of gen/agen/ogen/tgen and fixes the mu generator and start by mu_seed, so the switches do not change the trajectory beyond CUDA atomic noise.

RNG stream separation: gen (order shuffle, pool picks, batches), agen (adv starts, bank-Ritz samples), ogen (views), tgen (random adv start only when there is no seed class). The order shuffle happens before resume, so the order is identical after resume.

HostBanks keep-index mapping: sample -> get maps j through keep for q, s and F consistently. The random sign sg is applied to q and F (linear), and sensitivities are left unsigned (even in q). Adv columns get NaN s and NaN F and are excluded from the tail Gram via kinds.

HostBanks.clean: same semantics as train2.clean_banks plus F. Class removal pops q/s/F/keep. The memo path (data source) reproduces keep/classes/removals. from_data checks F and sens shapes against q.

bank_ritz math: W = V diag(max(ev, floor*evmax))^-1/2, top eigenvectors of W^T G_hat W, rescaled by c^T G c with the unfloored G. The returned ritz values are exact Rayleigh quotients X^T S_hat X / X^T S X (field is linear, G = Q^T S Q), so they are true lower bounds on mu. Near-null directions of G (dependent samples, e.g. low-rank macro) give Qc≈0 and hence G_hat≈0, so the floor keeps them out of the top set. bank_cols draws distinct samples per class while the bank allows.
tail_loss: eigvalsh backward involves no eigengap division. clamp_min(1) zeroes the gradient for lambda<1. The floored G only lowers lambda in near-null directions.
quota_counts always returns counts summing to B, with floor/floor+1 per class (the only issue is the inclusion bias, TRAINER-5).

Prefetch thread: it does host-only work (torch.load to CPU, mmap, finiteness scan). self.res is read only after join. log() is lock-protected. _CLEAN writes are idempotent per case. cancel() joins before reuse. There is no pinned memory (move() uses blocking .to, and HostBanks.get copies pageable memory).

Pool/DOF cap: admit evicts the oldest members while summed DOFs + incoming > cap. Resume rebuild from qi-P reproduces the same most-recent-that-fit set. Val and probe slots are dropped after evaluation unless they are pool members, and pool members wait on the host during eval.

O_h view handling in Slot: _shared attribute re-pointing after moves is correct (C is shared by object; the replaced tensors RP/RA/P/dM32 are re-pointed by name). Adversarial buffers are stored in the original frame, so they stay valid across different views on later visits. Val geometries never get a view and are never trained (no view leakage into selection).
batch_loss with defaults reproduces train2's loss op for op (log e_hat mean + sens_w * mean rho^2). The non-finite loss/grad guards skip the step without an EMA update.
stratified_probes draws only from train cases and terminates. mu_start is fixed per eval (seeded), so mu is comparable across evals within a run.

items.claim: With oh=true every pool entry trains on a random view out of 48, but evaluate() scores, computes mu and picks best.pt on the identity view only. best.pt from any v2 O_h run is therefore chosen by a metric that works against what the augmentation optimises.

In evaluate(), for each val and probe geometry and each k: v = OH.view(model, s_.geo, k) (k=0 -> s_.geo), res[w][kind][f'{case}@oh{k}'] = eval_geo(v, s_.banks, ...), then OH.drop(model, v). Take the family aggregate per view and make score = mean over views of the family score (optionally + worst view), with the identity score logged separately. Store eval_views and the per-view scores in best.pt / last.pt. Run mu/cert on the identity view, or on one fixed rotated view, to limit cost. The c_oh arm (g_cfg.sh: oh=True, ema=0.9997, eval_every=5000) did pick its 5k checkpoint, which is about 2x worse on rotated views (V2 doc section 1). Nothing in EVAL shows rotated-view error. As a result: (a) new v2 classes in mix with the default bank_source 'slot' (the slot cache has only the 5 old classes) are silently never trained; (b) glued and support_k are skipped per geometry by prep_geo2, so those geometries silently get more of the other classes; (c) 'adv' disappears for a geometry after ADV_FAIL or when adv_on_load is off.

The BUILD log line (train3 L164) lists the classes but nothing compares them to mix.
items.consequence: A v2 'new data' arm launched without bank_source='data' trains exactly like the control and reports no error. Its default score_classes also contains the absent classes, which score() skips. Per-geometry reweighting changes exposure per class in ways that are not logged per geometry.

Raise if strict_mix is set, or always raise when a mix class is missing from every geometry (for example new classes with bank_source 'slot'). Log 'adv' drops (no buffer) in the STEP counts, which already exist, and in an event.
